 Allegro MicroSystems, Entegris, Photronics, and Amtech shares skyrocket, what you need to know
 By:
 StockStory 
 November 03, 2026 at 13:15 PM EST 
 ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness. 
 What happened? 
 A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after investors returned to major chipmakers following steep previous-session declines and an aggregate $3.7 trillion sell-off sparked by concerns over artificial intelligence spending and neocloud debt. 
 As reported by CNBC, the rebound brought relief across the semiconductor landscape, lifting key players including Nvidia, AMD, and Intel alongside the broader Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. The sector had faced intense downward pressure in prior sessions, weighed down by growing skepticism surrounding massive corporate outlays on artificial intelligence infrastructure and the sustainability of neocloud debt, which refers to financing raised by specialized cloud providers to purchase advanced computing hardware. 
Despite these ongoing questions about the ultimate returns on enterprise AI spending, bargain hunters and institutional buyers stepped back into the market to scoop up shares at more attractive valuations after the historic retreat. 
 The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. 
 Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

 Zooming in on Allegro MicroSystems (ALGM)
 Allegro MicroSystems’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 55 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business. 
 The previous big move we wrote about was 7 days ago when the stock gained 6.4% on the news that major artificial intelligence deals and landmark financing agreements reinforced investor confidence in sustained technological demand as reported by AP News. Market sentiment received a major boost following news that Broadcom obtained $63 billion in bank financing to develop proprietary artificial intelligence chips for Anthropic. 
The massive commitment, paired with Anthropic filing for an initial public offering and Meta launching an equity offering, signaled to Wall Street that capital expenditure across the technology landscape remains robust. 
 For chipmakers and hardware designers, these multi-billion-dollar transactions demonstrate that major tech players continue to channel enormous financial resources into specialized infrastructure. 
Rather than slowing down, corporate appetite for computing power is accelerating, helping lift semiconductor shares and providing essential support to broader equity benchmarks such as the S&P 500.
 Allegro MicroSystems is up 27.2% since the beginning of the year, but at $34.24 per share, it is still trading 50.8% below its 52-week high of $69.62 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Allegro MicroSystems’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,077.
